processing: Hand-picked buds of Yunnan large-leaf tea are rolled by hand into small coils and made as black tea.
harvest_season: Not fixed by any standard; pure-bud lots depend on spring and other flushes that give plump buds, and spring is usually the most prized, as with other Dian Hong.
appearance_dry: Small, tight golden snails of pure bud, fuzzy to the touch.
appearance_wet: Plump, soft buds of golden copper, slowly uncoiling.
taste_profile: Sweet honey and a smooth texture, with a light fruity aroma and a long, pleasant finish.

brewing.notes: Western style, makers suggest a heaped teaspoon per 250 to 300 ml at 95 to 100 °C for 3 to 5 minutes, then decanting. Gongfu with cooler water is gentler on the buds.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year, like most fine Dian Hong, and best within a couple of years while the honey aroma is lively. Sellers often distinguish pure-bud lots from one-bud-one-leaf versions, so check which you are buying.
description:
Dian Hong Jin Luo is a Yunnan black tea with a shape you remember. Jin Luo means golden snail, and that's what the coiled buds look like. It comes from Simao in Pu'er, in south-west Yunnan.

It uses buds of the same large-leaf variety that goes into much of the region's pu-erh. Hand-rolling turns them into little coils, and because it is all bud, the coils come out gold, not the near-black of ordinary black tea.

The cup is amber, honey-sweet and smooth, with a light fruitiness and a finish that lingers. Pour off the tea promptly when brewing longer Western steeps; decanting softens any bitterness.

What Western shops call Yunnan Pure Bud Golden Snail is this tea. A very similar tea made with one leaf and a bud also exists, so look closely: more gold, more bud.

Compare it with a Bi Luo Chun style Hong Cha to see how much difference the bud-to-leaf ratio makes.
history: Little is documented about who first made Jin Luo or when. It belongs to the wider family of Dian Hong, and the snail shape seems to be a modern refinement in which makers applied hand-rolling skills to pure buds, though this is an impression, not a record.
